content.name: X4 Toolkit Helper
content.description: EXPERIMENTAL - use a throwaway save, not one you are playing. Companion for the X4 community toolkit's x4live command: it lets an external tool ask the RUNNING game questions without a quit-and-relaunch, and change exactly one thing about it. WHAT IT WRITES, all of it: (a) your profile's uidata.xml, via SaveUIUserData, twice per game load - UI userdata, not game state; (b) the game's PAUSE state, and only when an external x4live pause or x4live unpause asks for it. pause refuses if the game is already paused; unpause undoes only a pause this channel made and refuses anyone else's; both report the state the engine reads back afterwards, never what they meant to do. Nothing else: it changes no SAVEGAME state and declares save=false, adds no content, patches no file, registers no menu and no MD script, and has no eval of any kind. It loads into a running game and its answers have been wrong before. TWO CHANNELS. (1) A named-pipe channel answering a fixed, enumerated vocabulary asked by an external process: read verbs, plus the two argument-free write verbs above. One read verb looks up C functions the game's own ui lua declares by name, to report whether the engine exports each; it never calls one and never declares one. Object inspection is restricted to ids the channel itself issued in the same session, because vanilla never passes a foreign id to the engine and its behaviour on one is unknown. Every reply declares its own byte length and checksum, and every enumeration caps its own reply and reports how many rows it omitted, because an over-long message does not truncate: it tears the pipe down. (2) A uidata probe that writes an engine snapshot to a saved variable, readable only while the game is CLOSED. The pipe channel needs Mod Support APIs (ws_2042901274) for its named-pipe lua; that dependency is OPTIONAL, so without it this addon still loads and the probe half still works while the pipe half reports that the api is unavailable. Enumeration is NOT a census: ownerless objects belong to no faction and are invisible to any owner query, hidden factions are opt-in, and name and sector are player-knowledge, so most rows come back Unknown while ids, positions, class and flags stay exact. Ids do not survive a UI reload, which the engine performs on a save load and on an alt-enter graphics change, and neither does the record of which pause this channel made: a pause made before a reload survives it, but is then undone in game only. The channel reports its load time so a refusal can say whether a reload is the likely cause.
